title: Sixteenth Dynasty of Egypt
capsule: The Sixteenth Dynasty of Egypt was a short-lived polity of the Second Intermediate Period, centered on Thebes in Upper Egypt, existing roughly between 1650 and 1580 BCE while the Hyksos Fifteenth Dynasty dominated the north. Scholars dispute whether its rulers were themselves Hyksos vassals or an independent Theban line; Kim Ryholt's 1997 analysis argues for the latter, identifying up to fifteen kings from the Turin King List. Nebiryraw I enjoyed a period of relative stability, but persistent Hyksos pressure and famine ultimately gave way to the consolidating Seventeenth Dynasty, which launched the war of reunification under Seqenenre Tao.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is poorly attested; the dynasty is reconstructed almost entirely from the Turin King List and scattered scarab evidence, and its geographic control within Upper Egypt remains uncertain.
